desc: Write a brute-force solution for small N to generate all reachable strings and use it for validation.
Test the solution on the provided samples and on random small cases by comparing with the brute-force results.
Test on more edge cases: e.g., S consisting of many repeated '()', deeply nested structures, and cases where children have multiple symmetric pairs.
Verify the correctness of the intersection heuristic on cases where sets might overlap but not be identical. Construct explicit examples to test.
If discrepancies are found, refine the heuristic for intersection sizes (e.g., by computing exact intersections for small subtrees or using a more robust canonical representation).
Ensure the tree compression correctly handles edge cases (e.g., when the root becomes a leaf).
Consider using a deterministic hash to avoid randomness in the final answer.
Derive the correct formula for the size of the set for a node given children's sets and intersection sizes. Verify with brute-force results for small trees.
Design a method to compute the intersection size of two sets generated by disjoint subtrees.
Implement an efficient solution for N up to 5000 using the tree DP with intersection computation, ensuring it runs in O(N^2) or better.
